questions.question: Describe the Earth's surface and say what surrounds the Earth.
questions.expected_answer: The Earth is a sphere made of rock. Its surface has land, water and air. Oceans and seas cover most of it, and the land is made up of seven continents and many islands. A thin layer of air surrounds the whole Earth.

questions.question: Explain why the Sun looks bigger and brighter than other stars, and why the Earth is just right for life.
questions.expected_answer: The Sun is the closest star to the Earth, while the other stars are much further away, so the Sun looks much bigger and brighter. The Earth is at just the right distance from the Sun, so it gets enough heat and light for plants to make food and for water to stay liquid, but not too much. Its air keeps it warm and blocks harmful rays.

questions.question: Explain why the Moon has phases, and describe a rocket as a system.
questions.expected_answer: The Sun always lights up half of the Moon. As the Moon travels around the Earth, we see different amounts of the sunlit half, so it seems to change shape, repeating every twenty-nine and a half days. A rocket is a system: the input is fuel, the process is burning the fuel and pushing hot gas out of the back, and the output is movement into space.
